analysis.title: Global Fund Manager Survey: A light hits the boom on the grey
key_insights: November FMS: investors are bullish on macro (3% expect a hard landing) and markets (cash 3.6%), but euphoria on the boom and AI has ended. Tech overweight was cut by the most since Jun'06 (net 37% to net 12%).
BofA stays tactically risk-off. The November FMS does not show enough investor fear to buy: cash fell and bull sentiment did not pull back much.

50% of investors now expect a soft landing, overtaking no landing at 42% for the first time since June. 3% expect a hard landing. 'Boom' expectations fell to 41% from 47% in October, which was the highest since Feb'22.
Net 14% expect global growth to weaken over the next 12 months (the most since Apr'26), versus net 4% last month. Net 32% expect lower global CPI, the lowest inflation expectations since Oct'24.

AI capex is the main micro message. A record net 38% say companies are overinvesting, only 16% want companies to raise capex (lowest since May'20), and 52% expect a hyperscaler capex cut within 6 months, up from 30% last month.
Top tail risks are AI-related: 'AI bubble' 34% and 'AI hyperscaler credit event' 31%. Inflation and disorderly bond yields, the top tail risk in October, have receded.
38% see AI hyperscaler bonds as the most likely source of a systemic credit event, 30% private credit, 15% government debt, 8% leveraged ETFs, 1% crypto.
Most crowded trades: long global semiconductors 39% (down from a 82% peak in Jul'26), short China stocks 14%, long Magnificent 7 12%, short Treasuries 10%.

Bond underweight was cut by 13ppt, the biggest monthly increase in bond allocation since Apr'25. Investors are net 23% underweight bonds, the least since Nov'25. A 10Y UST yield of 5.8% (weighted average) would prompt a shift from stocks to bonds, 34% say 6.0% is needed.
A record net 23% say gold is undervalued.
Consumer short-covering: combined discretionary and staples allocation had the biggest monthly jump since Jun'06. Net underweight discretionary is 20% (from 34%) and staples 18% (from 32%).
Healthcare overweight rose to net 34% from 23%. Energy underweight widened to net 12% from net 4% overweight, materials went to net 9% underweight (most since Nov'25).
Equity allocation is net 41% overweight (from 44%). Cash allocation is net 9% underweight (from neutral). Investors reduced allocation to tech, USD, cash and Japan.
For 2027, 36% expect international equities to be the best asset class, 24% US equities, 17% gold. Nasdaq and MSCI EM tie at 21% as best index, and 42% pick the yen as best currency.
FMS year-end 2027 targets: UST 10Y 4.9% (current 5.1%), EURUSD 1.12 (current 1.10), S&P 500 7,926 (current 7,562), gold $4,341/oz (current $3,868).

BofA Cash Rule is at 3.6%, a Sell signal (sell at or below 4.0%). The Bull & Bear Indicator is 7.4, Neutral (sell above 8.0). Contrarian trades from extreme positioning: long cash/gold vs short stocks, long consumer vs short health care, long REITs vs short banks, long energy vs short industrials.
47% of investors describe the 12-month global economy as 'stagflation' (below-trend growth, above-trend inflation) versus 41% 'boom'.

Net 40% say USD is overvalued (from 36%), net 10% say EUR is undervalued. Investors are net 13% overweight US equities, net 28% overweight EM (from 34%), net 5% underweight Eurozone, net neutral Japan (from 9% overweight), net 21% underweight UK.

risk_factors: AI bubble is the top tail risk at 34%, followed by an AI hyperscaler credit event at 31%.
Consensus bear risk: global rate hikes leading to recession. Consensus bull risk: tech credit event concerns fading.
AI hyperscaler bonds (38%) and private credit (30%) are seen as the most likely sources of a systemic credit event.
52% expect an AI hyperscaler capex cut within 6 months, which would hit the AI-linked trades that investors still hold, such as long semiconductors.
Net 14% expect weaker global growth, the most since Apr'26.
charts_described: Chart 1 plots the net % overweight tech MoM change, showing the largest cut since Jun'06.
Chart 9 shows 52% of investors expect an AI hyperscaler capex cut in the next 6 months, versus 30% last month.
Chart 12 shows long global semiconductors as the most crowded trade at 39%, down from an 82% peak in Jul'26.
Chart 13 shows a record net 23% saying gold is undervalued.
Chart 15 shows 34% say a 6.0% 10Y yield is needed to shift into bonds, 30% say 5.5%, 16% say already at such levels.
vol_and_positioning: FMS cash level fell to 3.6% from 3.9%, the lowest since Aug'26. The BofA Cash Rule signal is Sell (sell at 4.0% or below, buy at 5.0% or above).
BofA Bull & Bear Indicator is 7.4 (Neutral, sell above 8.0). The broader sentiment measure fell to 6.3 from 6.4, the least bullish since Jun'26.

Long global semiconductors remains the most crowded trade at 39%, down from the 82% Jul'26 peak. Short China stocks is 14%, long Magnificent 7 12%, short Treasuries 10%, long US dollar 8%, long oil 5%.
Investors are taking net 4% more risk than normal... actually lower than normal: the report says net 4% lower than normal risk levels, from net 9% last month.
The FMS Financial Market Stability Risks Indicator rose to -0.6 from -0.9. Four of seven risk factors increased: emerging market, credit risk, business cycle, counterparty.
Net 71% expect high-quality earnings to beat low-quality, net 38% large caps to beat small caps, net 36% high dividend yield to beat low yield, net 35% low volatility to beat high volatility.

tension_points.bull_case: Investors still hold long semiconductors as the most crowded trade (39%), and BofA lists fading tech credit event concerns as the consensus bull risk.
tension_points.bear_case: 52% expect a hyperscaler capex cut within 6 months, a record net 38% say companies are overinvesting, and 38% see hyperscaler bonds as the most likely credit event source.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hyperscaler announcing a capex cut within the next 6 months, or the fading of tech credit event concerns, which BofA names as the bull risk.

tension_points.bull_case: Investors are bullish on macro (3% expect a hard landing), expect international equities to be the best 2027 asset and the S&P 500 at 7,926 by end-2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Cash at 3.6% triggers the BofA Cash Rule Sell signal and there is not enough investor fear to buy, so BofA stays tactically risk-off.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Cash at or above 5.0% would flip the BofA Cash Rule to Buy, and the Bull & Bear Indicator below 2.0 would signal a buy.
